zh.principle: **标准**：批准哈希算法的使用建议（SP 800-107）（Recommendation for Applications Using Approved Hash Algorithms (SP 800-107 Rev.摘要交代它管什么：「This document provides security guidelines for achieving the required or desired security strengths when using cryptographic applications that employ the approved hash functions specified in Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 180-4.」受影响的用法随即列出：「These include functions such as digital signatures, Keyed-hash Message Authentication Codes (HMACs) and Hash-based Key Derivation Functions (Hash-based KDFs).」它规定的是强度匹配，不规定哈希算法本身。引文的对象是强度而非算法本身：函数由 FIPS 180-4 指定，这份文件处理的是这些用法在达到所需强度时应当怎样取值与取舍。
zh.why: 出发点是最基本的那一步：「A hash algorithm is used to map a message of arbitrary length to a fixed-length message digest.」风险在于强度的错觉，§4.2 给出一般规律：「the expected collision resistance strength of any approved hash function is, in general, half the length of its hash value.」并记下已被攻破的例外：「The latest cryptanalytic results for SHA-1 [SHA1 Attack] indicate that it may have a collision resistance strength that is considerably less than its expected strength of 80 bits.」三段连读即是理由：把任意长消息压成固定摘要本身不是问题，把摘要长度当作强度才是；一般规律是碰撞抗性为摘要长之一半，而文件对冲着说 SHA-1 的实测结果可能远低于其 80 位期望强度（原文 indicate that it may have），并未把它写成已经确认的事实。
zh.used: §5.3.2 是给实现者的硬性要求，三条连读即可：「An HMAC key shall have a security strength that meets or exceeds the security strength required to protect the data over which the HMAC is computed.」「The HMAC key shall be kept secret.」以及「HMAC keys shall be generated as specified in SP 800-133 [SP 800-133].」三条都是 shall 级：强度须不低于所保护数据的要求，密钥须保密，生成方法则交由另一份文件规定，密钥生成本身不在本文件内给出。
zh.broken: §2 的符合性段承认有些要求验证程序覆盖不到：「Some of these requirements may be out-of-scope for CAVP and CMVP validation testing, and thus are the responsibility of entities using, implementing, installing, or configuring applications that incorporate this Recommendation.」§1 又划出两份 KDF 文件不在讨论之列：「these documents sufficiently address the security aspects of their use, so discussions of SP 800-56C and SP 800-108 are not included herein.」§5.2 对 SHA-1 设了有时效的限制：「SHA-1 shall not be used in any new digital signature applications that require at least 80 bits of security strength.」三处限制的层次不同：验证程序覆盖不到的要求由使用与配置方负责，两类 KDF 文件被明确排除在讨论之外，对 SHA-1 的禁止按用途与强度门槛起算。
zh.history: 扉页按本份文本自陈为「NIST Special Publication 800-107」的 Revision 1，标题行是「Recommendation for Applications Using Approved Hash Algorithms」，作者与部门两行连读为「Quynh Dang Computer Security Division Information Technology Laboratory」；题页标签按行序再连读即得日期「Information Technology Laboratory COMPUTER SECURITY August 2012」，也就是这份副本标注 2012 年 8 月，且不含 DOI 行。致谢页给出单作者与咨询者名单：「The author, Quynh Dang of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) gratefully appreciates the contributions and comments from Elaine Barker, William E.Burr, Shu-jen Chang, Lily Chen, Donna F.Dodson, Morris Dworkin, John Kelsey, Ray Perlner, W.Timothy Polk and Andrew Regenscheid.」附录 B 记下初版时间与本次修订内容：「The original version of this document was published in February 2009.」其条目之一为「Adding and addressing the security properties of SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256.」

en.principle: **Standard**: Recommendation for Applications Using Approved Hash Algorithms (SP 800-107 Rev. 1) (批准哈希算法的使用建议（SP 800-107）). The abstract states its subject: "This document provides security guidelines for achieving the required or desired security strengths when using cryptographic applications that employ the approved hash functions specified in Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 180-4." The affected uses follow at once: "These include functions such as digital signatures, Keyed-hash Message Authentication Codes (HMACs) and Hash-based Key Derivation Functions (Hash-based KDFs)." It governs strength matching, not the hash algorithms themselves. The quoted object is strength rather than the algorithms: the functions are designated by FIPS 180-4, and this document deals with how the listed applications reach the strength they require.
en.why: The starting point is the basic step: "A hash algorithm is used to map a message of arbitrary length to a fixed-length message digest." The risk is an illusion of strength, and §4.2 gives the rule of thumb: "the expected collision resistance strength of any approved hash function is, in general, half the length of its hash value." It then records the exception that has already fallen: "The latest cryptanalytic results for SHA-1 [SHA1 Attack] indicate that it may have a collision resistance strength that is considerably less than its expected strength of 80 bits." The three sentences form the argument: compressing an arbitrary message to a fixed digest is not the problem, treating digest length as strength is. The rule of thumb is collision resistance at half the digest length, and the document hedgingly reports that SHA-1 "may have" a collision resistance considerably below its expected 80 bits — it does not state that as a settled fact.
en.used: Section 5.3.2 states the implementer obligations in three sentences: "An HMAC key shall have a security strength that meets or exceeds the security strength required to protect the data over which the HMAC is computed." "The HMAC key shall be kept secret." and "HMAC keys shall be generated as specified in SP 800-133 [SP 800-133]." All three are shall-level: the strength must match the protected data, the key must stay secret, and key generation is handed to another document rather than specified here.
en.broken: The conformance paragraph in §2 admits that validation cannot cover everything: "Some of these requirements may be out-of-scope for CAVP and CMVP validation testing, and thus are the responsibility of entities using, implementing, installing, or configuring applications that incorporate this Recommendation." Section 1 also excludes two key-derivation documents: "these documents sufficiently address the security aspects of their use, so discussions of SP 800-56C and SP 800-108 are not included herein." And §5.2 places a dated restriction on SHA-1: "SHA-1 shall not be used in any new digital signature applications that require at least 80 bits of security strength." The three limits operate at different levels: requirements validation cannot reach become the responsibility of those who deploy and configure them, two key-derivation documents are excluded from discussion, and the SHA-1 prohibition is keyed to the use and the strength threshold.
en.history: Its own masthead makes this copy "NIST Special Publication 800-107" Revision 1, titled "Recommendation for Applications Using Approved Hash Algorithms", with the author and division lines reading in sequence as "Quynh Dang Computer Security Division Information Technology Laboratory"; continuing line by line through the title block gives "Information Technology Laboratory COMPUTER SECURITY August 2012", so this copy is dated August 2012 and contains no DOI line. The acknowledgements name the single author and the reviewers: "The author, Quynh Dang of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) gratefully appreciates the contributions and comments from Elaine Barker, William E. Burr, Shu-jen Chang, Lily Chen, Donna F. Dodson, Morris Dworkin, John Kelsey, Ray Perlner, W. Timothy Polk and Andrew Regenscheid." Appendix B gives the first edition date and one revision item: "The original version of this document was published in February 2009." and "Adding and addressing the security properties of SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256."

zh: message digest：哈希函数对任意长消息算出的固定长度输出。
truncated message digest：取全长度摘要左端若干比特的缩短结果。
collision resistance：难以找到产生同一摘要的两个消息，期望强度为摘要长之半。
preimage resistance：难以由摘要值求得能产生它的消息。
MacTag：HMAC 的输出标记，截断使用时不得少于 32 比特。
Hash-based KDF：以批准哈希或 HMAC 派生密钥材料的函数。
en: Message digest: the fixed-length output of a hash function over an arbitrary-length message.
Truncated message digest: the shortened result taken from the left end of the full digest.
Collision resistance: the difficulty of finding two messages with one digest, half the digest length in expectation.
Preimage resistance: the difficulty of recovering a message from its digest value.
MacTag: the HMAC output value, with a 32-bit floor when truncated.
Hash-based KDF: a key derivation function built on an approved hash function or HMAC.
